newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former banker Messier turns French media baron.
newsitem.headline: Former banker Messier turns French media baron.

text.p: Jean-Marie Messier, the young head of Generale des Eaux, could add the tag of "Media Baron" to a long list of titles as his firm prepared to announce on Thursday it was taking a 30 percent stake in Havas.

Set to become biggest shareholder in Havas, with activities ranging from travel to advertising, Generale was also set to become the main indirect holder in Europe's largest pay-TV group, the merged company of Canal Plus and Nethold.
A source confirmed to Reuters ahead of a news conference by Generale and Havas later on Thursday that the complex deal to take a large stake Havas had been agreed.

Messier, at 40 the youngest chairman of a French blue-chip company, had already earned accolades of expert government finance adviser and brilliant banker before joining Generale des Eaux in November 1994 with an eye on replacing Guy Dejounay at the helm of the water and services conglomerate.

Despite the reluctance of Generale des Eaux supervisory board members like Jacques Calvet, who is himself chairman of PSA Peugeot Citroen, to give the post and high pay package to a banker, Messier was made number two and later took the helm when Dejouany retired at 75 in June 1996.

Even before Dejounay had left the central-Paris office from which he controlled his empire for 20 years, Messier had taken on sensitive strategic issues and started to kick an ailing conglomerate back into shape.
The company, the biggest office owner in the La Defense business district in Paris, had been hit hard by property losses after the bottom fell out of the market at the end of the 1980s.
Messier launched an operation to buy out minorities in the ailing property unit Compagnie Immobiliere de Phenix, cleaned up its books and merged it into the parent group.

He took big charges for property losses, plunging Generale into the red in 1995, and brought in an experienced manager, Michel Lefebvreas head of the division after buying the George V property fund from entrepreneur Bernard Arnault.
Under Messier, Generale sold its stakes in Accor and its remaining interest in retailer FNAC and its 15 percent stake in exhibition organiser Blenheim.
He also streamlined the water and services activities.

But he did not limit his task to cost-cutting and asset stripping and unveiled an ambitious strategy to become France's second biggest telephone operator after France Telecom when the French market is liberalised in 1998.

In late 1995, he announced a complex deal under which British Telecom Plc, Mannesmann AG and SBC Communications became partners in a new telecoms holding company Cegetel while at the same time Alcatel Alsthom could sell its holding in mobile operator SFR.
The deal surprised analysts at the time because Generale des Eaux, under Dejouany, had been an ally to the Unisource venture of European's telecoms groups and AT & T.

On Thursday, a source confirmed he was set to announce the transfer of the company's media interests in Canal Plus, Canalsatellite and Generale des Images to Havas in order to strengthen the group's media clout and prepare an assault on the emerging multimedia market.

Jean-Marie Raymond Pierre Messier was born on December 13, 1956, in Grenoble. He pursued the educational path of France's high fliers through the Ecole Polytechnique and the Ecole Nationale d'Administration (ENA) before joining the Finance Ministry in 1986 on the privatisation team of Eduoard Balladur.

In 1989, he joined investment bank Lazard Freres, where he was soon seen as a candidate to replace Michel David-Weil at the helm of the blue-blooded bank, before leaving and moving a few streets away to Generale des Eaux.
Messier is married to Antoinette Fleisch and they have five children.
